current_answer: Jev is TypeSafe AI's hosted model for bounded Choice, Score and Noul judgments; your code must check each answer and own the action, review and fallback. As of 3 October 2026, 05:16 UTC, Jev is available to new users: signups have been open since 27 September (TypeSafe CEO's post), new accounts get no free credit, and the API is operational (status page); the pool did not observe signup itself because the console returns HTTP 403. TypeSafe lists jev-1.13.0 at $0.042 per million input tokens with free output; its published rate limits are now 100K tokens per second and 80 requests per second (the request limit was 40 per second from 30 September until at least 2 October 05:14 UTC; the exact time of the change is unknown). OpenRouter, Cloudflare, Vercel, Netlify and Opper serve it at the same or rounded list price, while lookalike reseller storefronts charged 3–16× that price. On the six routes whose data terms were read, no primary text allows training on your prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants it a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and to monitor for fraud and abuse, states no retention period and offers zero data retention to enterprise customers, while OpenRouter, Cloudflare and Vercel label the TypeSafe provider zero-retention and Vercel also routes Jev through DigitalOcean, which it marks as not zero-retention (a reading of the text, not legal advice). Published benchmarks, all Reported and graded A–D, disagree because they test different tasks: Jev is usually ahead of cheap LLM setups, close to frontier LLM judges on verdicts that can be read off the text once a threshold is tuned, and behind the best LLMs on derived judgments; TypeSafe's published 67.8% is agreement with LLM reference answers, not accuracy against human labels. No published moderation accuracy for Jev was found. Among open alternatives, only Opper's 362-item test puts one open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev (Opper hosts Kev); JevBench scores Laya and earlier Kev previews well below Jev. Code read at pinned commits shows how projects handle Jev failures: of five support-ticket triage projects, four send unsure tickets to a person and one files tickets in its archive lane on any Jev API error; of six self-hosted Jev model routers, one sends every Jev failure to its frontier model and five keep the current model, pick locally or choose no model, while OpenRouter does not document what its Jev Router does when Jev fails; of six moderation projects, four leave the post up or let it through when the Jev call fails, one holds it for a person and one returns no decision; of five email and lead sorters, none changes the mailbox when Jev errors, and of the 3 that can write to Gmail or IMAP only 1 routes unsure mail to a Review label. Python and TypeScript have official SDKs (typesafe-sdk 0.7.2, @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0); of five Claude Code and MCP guardrails read in source, only LangChain's AutoModeMiddleware fails closed, @jkudish/jev-mcp 0.13.0 keeps its audited advisory failure path, and oh-my-claudecode v5.6.0 keeps its failure path with a 2,000 ms default timeout (250 ms up to v5.5.0). TypeSafe's own n8n node is the scoped @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai (npm provenance, n8n-verified); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai is a third party's, and all 5 n8n nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error by default. Of 61 Products ledger rows, the pool read the Jev call in source for 39; none of the 61, nor 7 published claims, is independently verified as running in production.

catalogue_card.question: What can I build with Jev, what alternatives exist, and where can I use it at what cost?
catalogue_card.text: Question-ordered pages on Jev (TypeSafe AI): current access status and notices, use cases including support-ticket triage, model routing, content moderation and email and lead sorting, demo videos, graded benchmarks, Jev vs Laya vs Kev, Jev vs LLM vs classifier, data retention and training by route, limits, build guides including the n8n node, errors, confidence thresholds, reseller checks, cost per decision, routes, projects and open alternatives, each with evidence labels and check dates.

summary: Access (checked 3 Oct 2026, 05:16 UTC): signups open since 27 Sep 2026, 22:33 UTC (CEO post); no free credit for new users; API operational since 29 Sep, 22:05 UTC (status page; 90-day API uptime 99.826%). The pool did not observe signup: the console returned HTTP 403.
Jev answers from a fixed answer set: Choice (up to 255 options), Score (up to 10 levels), Noul (probability of yes). It does not generate text and accepts text input only.

List price $0.042/M input, output free on TypeSafe, OpenRouter, Cloudflare and (in its models API) Vercel; Opper and Vercel's web page round to $0.04; Netlify bills credits. Lookalike resellers displayed 3–16× the list price.

TypeSafe's published rate limits are 100K tokens per second and 80 requests per second (checked 3 Oct, 05:16 UTC). The request limit was 40 per second from 30 Sep until at least 2 Oct, 05:14 UTC; before 30 Sep the page listed 250,000 tokens/s and 1,200 requests/min. Neither change has an exact time.

Data handling (quoted 1 Oct, not legal advice): no route's text allows training on prompts without consent; TypeSafe's MCA grants a licence in perpetuity to use Customer Data to derive telemetry and to monitor for fraud and abuse; no TypeSafe retention period is stated; ZDR is offered directly to enterprise customers.

Zero data retention by layer: OpenRouter's gateway is ZDR by default and lists the TypeSafe endpoint as ZDR; Cloudflare lists ZDR 'Yes' but AI Gateway logs are on by default; Vercel marks TypeSafe AI ZDR but also routes Jev through DigitalOcean, marked not ZDR; Opper says ZDR is not established for its TypeSafe route.

Jev vs Laya vs Kev: only Opper's 362-item test (B11) puts an open model, Kev-4B, within noise of Jev, and Opper hosts Kev; JevBench (B07) scores Laya 23.0–41.7 and earlier Kev previews 53.8–59.7 against Jev's 80.0. All Reported.

Laya and Kev weights are Apache-2.0; Kev's Qwen bases are Apache-2.0; Laya's card metadata names no base. Laya's English checkpoint reads 512 tokens and its multilingual checkpoint ships uncalibrated; Kev is English-only.

Support-ticket triage, five projects read at pinned commits: four gate on confidence (0.5–0.9) and send unsure tickets to a person; one ignores queue confidence and archives tickets on API errors; only one validates answers; two set no timeout.

Model routing (2 Oct): OpenRouter documents how its Jev Router narrows candidates, but not what it does when Jev fails, is unsure or gets a long conversation, nor how the routed model is billed. Of six self-hosted Jev routers read at pinned commits (chosen by GitHub stars), one sends every Jev failure to its frontier model; one keeps the current model; two pick locally; two choose no model.

Content moderation (2 Oct): of six projects read at pinned commits (five code-backed integrations, one runnable demo), four leave the post up or let it through when the Jev call fails, one holds it for a person (WordPress) and one returns no decision. Two have a pardon that lifts the punishment but does not restore the message; four send author data beyond the text by default. No published moderation accuracy was found.

Email and lead sorting (3 Oct): of 5 sorters read at pinned commits (chosen by GitHub stars plus one lead project), none changes the mailbox when Jev errors; 3 can write to the mailbox and only 1 of those sends unsure mail to a Review label; none has delete or trash code. Cost per 1,000 emails by pool arithmetic: about $0.04–$0.15 at the projects' body cuts; a Reported demo works out to $0.106.

Benchmarks: 14 tier-1 studies and 10 shorter rows graded A–D with flags; all results Reported; the pool ran none. TypeSafe's 67.8% is agreement with LLM reference answers, not accuracy against human labels.

Build: typesafe-sdk 0.7.2; @typesafe-ai/sdk 0.6.0 or AI SDK experimental_evaluate (audited at ai 7.0.122; 7.0.127 released 1 Oct, not re-audited). Claude Code and MCP guardrails: only LangChain AutoModeMiddleware fails closed; @jkudish/jev-mcp 0.13.0 keeps the audited failure path; oh-my-claudecode v5.6.0 keeps its failure path, defaults to a 2,000 ms timeout (250 ms up to v5.5.0) and adds OMC_JEV=<point>:active, which lets Jev decide.

n8n (3 Oct): TypeSafe's node is the scoped @typesafe-ai/n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai 0.9.0 (npm provenance to typesafe-ai tag 0.9.0; the only Jev node verified on n8n); the unscoped n8n-nodes-typesafe-ai belongs to a third party. All 5 nodes read stop the workflow on a Jev error unless Continue On Fail is on.

46 creator videos show Jev running on concrete tasks in 13 use-case groups. Products ledger (3 Oct): 61 rows, 39 grade A (Jev call read in source); 7 company and analyst production or cost claims listed, 5 rechecked on 3 Oct and 2 relayed by VentureBeat not rechecked; none is independently verified.
uncertainty: No pool-made Jev call, account, bill, signup, mailbox connection or package install; the console returned HTTP 403 on 3 Oct. X could not be searched for newer TypeSafe posts.

TypeSafe's subprocessor list and any SOC 2 report sit behind a script-only trust page and were not read; whether DigitalOcean on Vercel forwards to TypeSafe, and whether OpenRouter's ZDR listing rests on a special agreement, are not stated; Netlify's data terms were not read.
A TypeSafe retention period, human access to inputs and a Telemetry opt-out are not stated in TypeSafe's public text.
Which Kev checkpoints JevBench ran, Kev-9B's base licence, the JevAny/AnyJev identity and the operator of he-jev are unknown.
The five triage projects are code-backed but none is verified as operating; at least 70 more triage repositories were not read.
No benchmark was run or rerun by the pool; four A grades are provisional; no graded comparison with a fine-tuned classifier exists with published materials.
ai 7.0.127 was not re-audited. The exact time of the 40-to-80 requests-per-second change is unknown (no archive capture since 1 Oct).

What OpenRouter's Jev Router does when Jev fails and how it bills the routed model are not documented; none of the six routers or six moderation projects read in source was run, and none is verified as operating.

Email: ilyamk's granted OAuth scope and spam-leadgen's no-key behaviour are unknown; three email projects set no HTTP timeout; whether question text is billed and the tokens-per-character ratio are assumptions. n8n: core error-output handling is known only from the official node's code comment; 10 of 15 n8n packages found were not read; the declined-verification claim is Reported. Two VentureBeat-relayed production claims were not rechecked.
Reddit, X, TikTok and YouTube could not be read in the daily scan; search analytics were unavailable when page topics were chosen (3 Oct run).
